Giving Tuesday 2025 pulled in $4 billion. Scammers noticed.

Giving Tuesday 2026 is Tuesday, December 1. US donations on the day grew from $1.97B in 2019 to $4.0B in 2025 (GivingTuesday Data Commons).
The copycat playbook: lookalike pages and posts, texts and emails with links, fake fundraisers, pay-by-app requests.
Example: a $50 gift to a real GoFundMe personal fundraiser loses 2.9% + $0.30 = $1.75, so $48.25 reaches the organizer. On a fake page, $0 reaches the cause.
BBB Wise Giving Alliance standard: at least 65% of expenses on programs.

Sources: GivingTuesday Data Commons; FTC consumer alert, 2025; California, North Carolina and Arizona attorneys general; BBB; GoFundMe pricing.
News and education, not financial advice.
Follow @financeprostv for money explained simply.

Americans gave $4.0 billion on Giving Tuesday 2025, up from $1.97 billion in 2019 (GivingTuesday Data Commons), and Giving Tuesday 2026 is December 1. The FTC (2025) and state attorneys general describe lookalike pages, texts and emails with links, fake fundraisers and pay-by-app requests; on a real GoFundMe a $50 gift nets $48.25 to the organizer after its 2.9% + $0.30 fee, while a fake page passes on $0. Sources: GivingTuesday, FTC, California AG, BBB Wise Giving Alliance, GoFundMe.

News and education, not financial advice.
